I give up. I did not change `/work/putnam_2007_b4.lean`.

The math is settled, but a formal proof is far beyond what I can finish here:

- **Answer:** the set has exactly 2^(n+1) elements. Write F = P + iQ. Then P² + Q² = F·F̄, so F is a factor of X^(2n)+1 over ℂ. The 2n roots split into n conjugate pairs. Choosing one root from each pair gives 2^n choices. Degree of P > degree of Q forces the unit constant to be ±1, giving 2^(n+1) total.
- **Why it is hard in Lean:** the proof needs (a) factoring X^(2n)+1 over ℂ with simple roots, (b) showing F·F̄ = X^(2n)+1 forces F to be a product over one root from each conjugate pair, (c) a degree argument that pins the constant to ±1, and (d) an injective map from the 2^(n+1) explicit choices onto the set, converting between ℂ[X] and ℝ[X]. That is several hundred lines of Mathlib work with many pitfalls, and I have not compiled any of it.
